newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude sharply lower after Gulf storm.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude sharply lower after Gulf storm.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude oil prices fell sharply after a tropical storm left a key production region in the Gulf of Mexico unscathed Friday, traders said.
Local sales of light grade Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude -- the regional benchmark -- remained flat Friday, with refiners shopping for foreign grades or cutting production.
Key seller BP continued to offer at $1.85 under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI)

Discounts for ANS remained $2.16 a barrel under WTI. With the discount flat, outright prices for ANS crude slid to $16.97/17.14 a barrel, in line with lower spot and futures oil prices throughout the U.S.
The drop came a day after oil prices rose sharply on fears Tropical Storm Danny would damage rigs that pump oil and natural gas in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico.
Light Line 63 crude also fell after fears of storm damage ended. The grade is trading minus $3.05 a barrel under WTI, and its price over Buena Vista stood unchanged at 90 cents to $1.00.
Meanwhile, Kern River and Wilmington crudes -- California heavy grades -- rose after major oil companies increased postings late Thursday and several local deals got done at smaller discounts.
